title: Reachability from Equal Register States
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean input word, $B$ a natural-number bound, $l$ an instruction label, and $	ext{st},	ext{st}'$ machine states with $	ext{st}=	ext{st}'$. Starting at label $l$ with register values given by $	ext{st}$ and no answer, the machine can reach label $l$ with register values given by $	ext{st}'$ and no answer, along a finite run in which every configuration before the endpoint satisfies the machine guard and has every register at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: The machine states satisfy st = st′.
replaced:
For any input bit string $x$, bound $B$, instruction label $l$, and register states
$\mathrm{st},\mathrm{st}'$ with $\mathrm{st}=\mathrm{st}'$, the machine can reach the
configuration with label $l$, the register values of $\mathrm{st}'$, and no answer,
starting from the configuration with label $l$, the register values of $\mathrm{st}$,
and no answer. Every configuration before the final step satisfies the machine's
preconditions and has all register values at most $B$.
